primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Inactivating GNAS-related defects can reduce Gs-alpha signaling downstream of the PTH receptor. Impaired stimulation of adenylyl cyclase lowers the cAMP response to PTH, producing end-organ PTH resistance despite elevated circulating PTH.
vignette: A 14-year-old girl is evaluated for intermittent muscle cramps. She has a round face, short stature, and shortening of the fourth and fifth metacarpals. Laboratory studies show hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and an elevated parathyroid hormone concentration; renal function is normal.
lead: Which intracellular signaling abnormality most directly explains these findings?
correct: Reduced Gs-alpha stimulation of adenylyl cyclase after PTH receptor activation
distractors: Reduced synthesis and secretion of PTH by parathyroid chief cells
Constitutive Gs-alpha activation with persistent adenylyl cyclase signaling
Increased calcium-sensing receptor activity that suppresses PTH release
Defective CYP27B1-mediated conversion of vitamin D to calcitriol
Excess FGF23 signaling that decreases renal phosphate reabsorption
distractor_notes: True hypoparathyroidism causes PTH deficiency; this patient's PTH is elevated, indicating hormone resistance rather than absent hormone production.
Constitutively active Gs-alpha signaling is associated with disorders such as McCune-Albright syndrome, the opposite signaling direction from GNAS-inactivation pseudohypoparathyroidism.
Gain-of-function CaSR variants increase calcium sensitivity and suppress PTH; they do not explain elevated PTH with an Albright hereditary osteodystrophy phenotype.
CYP27B1 deficiency impairs calcitriol production and can cause hypocalcemia, but vitamin D-dependent rickets is characterized by low phosphate rather than the hyperphosphatemia of PTH resistance.
Excess FGF23 lowers serum phosphate by reducing renal phosphate reabsorption; it therefore conflicts with this patient's hyperphosphatemia.
key_expl: Hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH, and Albright hereditary osteodystrophy features indicate pseudohypoparathyroidism with end-organ PTH resistance. In GNAS-related disease, impaired Gs-alpha signaling reduces activation of adenylyl cyclase and generation of cAMP after PTH receptor stimulation. The circulating PTH level rises because target tissues fail to respond normally.
objective: Recognize pseudohypoparathyroidism from hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH, and Albright hereditary osteodystrophy, and link it to impaired Gs-alpha–adenylyl cyclase–cAMP signaling.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Pseudohypoparathyroidism and Related Disorders
sources.locator: Continuing Education Activity; Introduction; Etiology; Pathophysiology
sources.support: NCBI describes pseudohypoparathyroidism as end-organ PTH resistance with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and elevated PTH, often with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy. It identifies GNAS/Gs-alpha defects and impaired PTH/PTHrP–Gs-alpha–cAMP signaling, in which PTH receptor activation normally stimulates Gs-alpha and intracellular cAMP generation.

sources.title: Disorders of GNAS Inactivation
sources.locator: Clinical Characteristics — PHP-Ia/PHP-Ic; Table 2 Phenotypes and Genetic Mechanisms
sources.support: GeneReviews defines pseudohypoparathyroidism as hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia caused by end-organ PTH resistance and describes Albright hereditary osteodystrophy features including short stature, round facies, and brachydactyly/brachymetacarpia.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Hypoparathyroidism
sources.support: NCBI states that true hypoparathyroidism is PTH deficiency and produces hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia, distinguishing deficient hormone secretion from PTH resistance with elevated PTH.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: GNAS gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — McCune-Albright syndrome; Other disorders
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that GNAS encodes the stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit that activates adenylyl cyclase. Activating GNAS variants cause constitutive signaling in McCune-Albright syndrome, whereas GNAS variants associated with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy can produce pseudohypoparathyroidism when endocrine resistance is present.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: CASR gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — Autosomal dominant hypocalcemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus explains that activating CASR variants make the receptor overly sensitive to calcium, suppressing PTH release and reducing renal calcium reabsorption, which can cause hypocalcemia.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Vitamin D-dependent rickets
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that CYP27B1 pathogenic variants impair conversion of vitamin D to calcitriol and that vitamin D-dependent rickets can produce low blood calcium and phosphate.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: X-linked hypophosphatemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus identifies excess FGF23 signaling as central to X-linked hypophosphatemia and explains that it reduces renal phosphate reabsorption, producing low serum phosphate rather than hyperphosphatemia.
